flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad, mostly impairments on wholesale loans this quarter.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and bonuses — Goldman's biggest cost by far, about 27 cents of every revenue dollar.

opex.name: Transaction based
opex.note: Costs that rise and fall with trading and deal volume: brokerage, clearing and exchange fees.

opex.name: Communications and technology
opex.note: Trading systems, market data and communications.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of offices, systems and equipment over their useful lives.

opex.name: Occupancy
opex.note: Rent and running costs for offices around the world.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Everything else — this quarter it includes significantly higher charitable contributions to Goldman Sachs Gives.

follow100Note: Almost half of every $100 (about $44) goes to the people — pay plus the transaction costs their deals generate. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Banks don't report gross profit; this chart follows Goldman Sachs' own structure — revenue, less credit costs, less running costs. By business: Global Banking & Markets earned $13,458M (+32%) and Asset & Wealth Management $5,051M (+14%); Platform Solutions shrank to $170M.
oneTimers: Platform Solutions revenue fell 72% to $170M, mostly on markdowns of the Apple Card loan portfolio (moved to held-for-sale in late 2025) — the last drag from Goldman's abandoned consumer push.
Provisions for litigation and regulatory proceedings were just $23M, versus $131M a year ago.
'Other expenses' jumped because charitable contributions to Goldman Sachs Gives were significantly higher — the firm's own presentation estimates the drag at roughly $1.00 of EPS.

segments.name: Noninterest revenues
segments.note: Trading and dealmaking: market making brought in $5,658M, investment banking $3,233M, investment management $4,102M, commissions $1,515M and other principal transactions $401M. Equities alone earned $6,441M, up 72%.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and trading assets, minus the interest Goldman pays to fund them — a small slice at Goldman compared with Main Street banks, and it shrank 2%.

takeaways.text: Equities revenue hit $6,441M — financing up 96% and intermediation up 52% — while FICC was flat at $3,471M. Clients traded and borrowed against stocks at a pace Goldman rarely sees.
takeaways.title: Equities carried the quarter

takeaways.text: Assets under supervision reached a record $4,097B, up from $3,452B a year ago, and Asset & Wealth Management fees rose 22%. Dealmaking helped too: investment banking fees of $3,224M rose 21%, with equity underwriting up 43%.
takeaways.title: The wealth business hit a record

takeaways.text: Platform Solutions — the remains of the consumer experiment — shrank to $170M of revenue on Apple Card markdowns. It's now less than 1% of the firm; the quarter shows Goldman fully back to its wholesale roots.
takeaways.title: The consumer hangover is nearly over

verdict: Goldman Sachs rode a trading and dealmaking boom to $18.7B of revenue (+23%) and $5.3B of profit — equities revenue jumped 72% — while its leftover consumer business shrank to almost nothing.
